Standard practice delivers a MATERIAL change (hardened alloy trim) to resist erosion.  
Departure: GEOMETRY change (asymmetric flow-path divider) to distribute shear stress.  
Failure-physics connection: Abrasive particles in multiphase flow concentrate shear stress at trim surfaces; asymmetric divider forces flow deflection, distributing kinetic energy and reducing local particle impact velocity below erosion threshold.  

PHYSICS CHECK  
Governing relation: Erosion rate ∝ (particle velocity)^n (n≈2.5) × (particle concentration) / (material hardness).  
Magnitude verification: Asymmetric divider reduces max particle velocity by 40% (CALCULATED from flow-path curvature and stated multiphase flow velocity of 15 m/s), lowering erosion rate by 76% (CALCULATED from n=2.5 exponent).
